title: Churning out nearly 500 tokens per second, the Zhipu GLM-5.3 High-Speed Edition has made a quiet debut.
key_facts: Zhipu has quietly begun testing its high-speed flagship model GLM-5.3 HighSpeed in its AI programming tool ZCode, ZheDongXi reports on 12 Oct 2026.
AI programming content creator 'Leo' on X says he was granted grayscale (limited test) access and that output speed can exceed 490 tokens per second.
Latest data from the AI Ping evaluation platform: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash official API output speed 121.34 tokens/s; Zhipu's official GLM-5.3 API 70.84 tokens/s.
GLM-5.3 HighSpeed is randomly open to ZCode subscription users only, with no clear sign-up for the internal test; the speed seen can serve only as a reference until an official launch.
It appeared on the website of the open-source programming agent Pi harness a month ago; input and output pricing is not disclosed.
Context window of 1 million tokens and up to 131,072 tokens of output at a time, consistent with GLM-5.3.
In May Zhipu launched a GLM-5.1-highspeed API for some enterprise users at about 400 tokens/s, built with the TileRT team through inference-engine, scheduling and infrastructure optimisation.
The article says raising inference speed, including for flagship models, is becoming a focus of competition.
quote_evidence: Recently, Zhipu has quietly launched the test of its high-speed flagship model GLM-5.3 HighSpeed in its AI programming tool ZCode.
GLM-5.3 HighSpeed is currently only randomly open to ZCode subscription users, and there is no clear entry for internal test application.

The extremely fast speed demonstrated during the internal test can only be used as a reference, and the final performance should be measured by its actual speed when it is officially launched and provides large-scale external services.
why_it_matters_hint: Faster output makes AI coding agents, which make many model calls in a row, noticeably quicker if the speed holds at launch.
event_date: Reported 12 Oct 2026; test access date not stated.
notes: Read 36Kr in full; it republishes ZheDongXi with authorization, so ZheDongXi is credited as the first reporter. The 490 tokens/s figure comes from one creator's limited-test access, not an official launch.
